course_title: Introduction to Principles of Physiotherapy Assessment and Management
course_description:
Emphasis on the importance of applied anatomy, physiology, biomechanics & psychology as key factors in physiotherapy diagnosis & treatment & introduction of a number of basic therapeutic movement, diagnostic & treatment skills.

This course is aimed at providing the student with a sound knowledge of kinesiology which forms the basis for physiotherapy diagnosis and treatment. The importance of applying anatomical knowledge is emphasised. Topics covered include: observation and analysis of movement of the head, neck, trunk, upper limbs and lower limbs; theory and practice of joint range measurement, passive movements, muscle strength testing and muscle length assessment.

Additional timetable information
This subject has an online, pre-recorded lecture which students should view weekly, and before their practical session.ﾠThere is also a 2 hour practical class each week with the year cohort divided into four practical class groups. Each student will haveﾠa practical class on Fridays at one of the allocated times: 8-10AM, 10-12PM, 12.30PM-2.30PM or 2.30PM-4.30PM. A tutorial will be held five times throughout the semester with the year cohort divided into four tutorial class groups. Please see tutorials dates and times in student timetables.
It is expected that students have revised the content to be covered in each practical and tutorial session beforehand. Tutors will not be demonstrating techniques in class, rather they will be providing feedback to students on their own performance during class. Students should schedule time each week for self-study and practical technique practice for this course. Availability of practical rooms, on a week-by-week basis, can be found at the Student Unit Reception on Level 3.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the roles of anatomy and kinesiology in physiotherapy assessment and management.
Identify key measurement principles in physiotherapy practice and research, and justify their importance in ensuring accuracy.
Effectively perform and explain basic muscle and joint assessment procedures, including manual muscle tests, goniometry, muscle length tests, and passive movements.
Demonstrate client-centred communication strategies to obtain informed consent, deliver client education, and share knowledge with the client and relevant others in a clear and collaborative manner.
Analyse human movement using basic anatomical, physiological, biomechanical, and psychological principles.
Apply problem-solving strategies to foundational clinical situations.
Demonstrate an ethical and professional approach to physiotherapy practice.
Apply ergonomic principles to handle and position clients, ensuring safety, effectiveness, comfort and to minimise risk to the client and the physiotherapist.

assessment_details.task_description: Practical examination covering all relevant practical techniques including measurements, manual muscle testing, passive movements and muscle length testing learned for Region 1 - the lower limb. Students will be required to perform various tests, measurements and/or treatments in a series of practical examinations. The emphasis in these examinations is on the EFFECTIVE and SAFE PERFORMANCE of these procedures, although examiners will also question students about the theory underlying the techniques. The criteria mark sheet for practical examinations is available on Blackboard in the assessment folder. Practical examinations will be scheduled on-campus in a face-to-face format. In this course the recording of an assessment (oral/practical) performance has been waived, a record of student performance will be taken by detailed written notes that can be referred to if a remark is required at a later date. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. learning_activities.topic: Region 1 - lower limb theory Weekly lectures are provided online, designed for self-paced learning. Weeks 1-5 will include content on assessment and management of lower limb.

Region 1 - lower limb practice Partcipants will attend a 2-hour in-person practical session on campus each week. To prepare, participants must complete online learning and associated preparatory tasks prior to attending. Region 1 will include practical classes on the lower limb.
Region 2 - spine theory Weekly lectures are provided online, designed for self-paced learning. Weeks 6-8 will include content on assessment and management of head, neck and trunk.

Region 2 - spine practice Partcipants will attend a 2-hour in-person practical session on campus each week. To prepare, participants must complete online learning and associated preparatory tasks prior to attending. Region 2 will include practical classes on the head, neck and trunk.
Region 3 - upper limb theory Weekly lectures are provided online, designed for self-paced learning. Weeks 8 -13 will include content on assessment and management of lower limb function.

Region 3 - upper limb practice Partcipants will attend a 2-hour in-person practical session on campus each week. To prepare, participants must complete online learning and associated preparatory tasks prior to attending. Region 3 will include practical classes on the upper limb.

Regions 1 - 3 - tutorials Tutorials will be delivered at scheduled times over the semester (please refer to student timetables for allocated times). Tutorials will include small group activities to improve learning, consolidation of knowledge and clinical reasoning.
